answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may claim rewards, with payouts weighted by stake-age and capped per verified task. A newcomer cannot multiply influence by minting accounts: each extra identity ties up more capital and must wait through the same maturation period. Audits that catch duplicated work slash the bond, making a sybil swarm expensive to maintain. In a karst of pseudonyms, the atlas of claims still needs a durable anchor: collateral at risk.
